readme.missing: <true or false depending on whether a readme file is present in the package>
readme.path: <path relative to `package/<package-id>/` to readme file in the package  - if applicable or 'N/A'>

manuscript.missing: <true or false depending on whether the manuscript is included in the package>
manuscript.title: <Title of the manuscript as specified in the readme or manuscript file - if applicable or 'N/A'>
manuscript.path: <path relative to `package/<package-id>/` to manuscript file in the package - if applicable or 'N/A'>

software.missing: <true or false depending on whether the software information is present in the readme>
software.version: <version of software used to run the code, e.g. Stata 18.0 MP, R 4.3.1, Python 3.11 - if applicable or 'N/A'>

run_instructions.missing: <true or false depending on whether information on how to run the code is present in the readme>
run_instructions.main_script: <path relative to `package/<package-id>/` to the main script that runs all other scripts - if applicable or 'N/A'>
run_instructions.details: <description of how to run the code as specified in the readme - if applicable or 'N/A'>

root_directory.missing: <true or false depending on whether the readme specifies which line in the main script to change for a new machine>
root_directory.details: <description of which line in the main script to change for a new machine as specified in the readme - if applicable or 'N/A'>

code_file_completeness.complete: <Describe whether the names of the code files suggests that all code files from raw data to all output are included in the package - give examples on what seems to be missing>
code_file_completeness.redundant: <Describe whether the names of the code files suggests that there are unnecessary code files (e.g., exploratory scripts, old versions) included in the package - give examples on what seems to be unnecessary>
